**Ravindra Jadeja** returns to the squad after recovering from tennis elbow.
The series runs **Galle (Aug 15–19)** then **Colombo (Aug 23–27)**.
cards.moot: Fitness-contingent squad selections are a normal part of managing fast bowlers' workloads — teams often name a player 'subject to fitness' rather than leave a match-winner out entirely, keeping options open until the last responsible moment.

thread.previously: We reported Bumrah was resting until July 30 before a fresh fitness test, with his Sri Lanka Test spot hinging on an August 7 practice match in Colombo.
thread.changed: Selectors have now named the full 15-man squad: Bumrah and Sai Sudharsan are included subject to BCCI fitness clearance, Ravindra Jadeja is back after recovering from tennis elbow, Washington Sundar is ruled out of the first Test with a hamstring injury, and 33-year-old offspinner Saransh Jain earns a maiden call-up in his place.

depth.why_it_matters: This is India's first full Test squad announcement since Bumrah's fitness scare, resolving weeks of uncertainty about who leads the bowling attack, while also handing a long-serving domestic cricketer his overdue India debut opportunity.
depth.ripple_effects: If Bumrah fails his fitness test, India's pace attack in Sri Lanka's spin-friendly conditions shifts significantly, likely leaning harder on spin options including Jain. cards.title: Ryan ten Doeschate returns to Knight Riders as head of cricket strategy across all franchises

That covers **Kolkata Knight Riders (IPL)**, **Trinbago Knight Riders (CPL)**, **Abu Dhabi Knight Riders (ILT20)** and **Los Angeles Knight Riders (MLC)**
He'll also serve as **assistant coach** for the CPL, ILT20 and MLC franchises in the group

Ten Doeschate previously won **two IPL titles as a KKR player (2012, 2014)** and a third as **support staff in 2024**

depth.background: Knight Riders Sports is the ownership group behind Kolkata Knight Riders and its sister T20 franchises in the Caribbean Premier League, ILT20 and Major League Cricket. Ten Doeschate's ties to the group go back to 2011 as a KKR player, and he later moved into coaching there in 2022 before joining India's men's team as assistant coach for two years, a post he has now left.

depth.why_now: The timing lines up with IPL franchises starting to plan for the 2027 retention window, expected to open around mid-September.

cards.title: Shubman Gill becomes India's fourth-ever No.1 ranked ODI batter as Siraj tops the bowling charts too
cards.what_happened: Following his performances in India's recent ODI series in England — including an unbeaten 80 in the first match and 77 at Lord's in the third — **Shubman Gill** overtook Babar Azam to claim the **No.1 spot in the ICC ODI batting rankings**, becoming just the fourth Indian to do so after Sachin Tendulkar, MS Dhoni and Virat Kohli. In the same rankings update, **Mohammed Siraj** rose to **No.1 among ODI bowlers**, giving India the top spot in both disciplines at once. Separately, 15-year-old **Vaibhav Suryavanshi** jumped 230 places in the T20I batting rankings, reflecting his rapid rise through IPL and youth-cricket performances.
key_points: **Shubman Gill** dethroned Babar Azam to become the world's **No.1 ranked ODI batter**.
**Mohammed Siraj** simultaneously rose to **No.1 among ODI bowlers**.
Gill is only the **fourth Indian ever** to hold the top ODI batting spot, after Tendulkar, Dhoni and Kohli.
The rise came on the back of Gill's England ODI series form, including scores of **80 not out and 77**.
Teenager **Vaibhav Suryavanshi jumped 230 places** in the T20I batting rankings on the same list update.
cards.moot: Rankings systems reward recent, high-quality performance against strong opposition more than raw career totals — which is why a single good series can move a player to No.1 quickly.

depth.background: The **ICC Player Rankings** are updated regularly using a points system that weighs recent performances, opposition strength and match context, and reaching No.1 in any format is considered one of the clearest statistical markers of a player's current form. Gill has been closing in on the top ODI spot for weeks; Babar Azam had held it before him.
depth.why_it_matters: Holding the world No.1 ranking in both ODI batting and bowling simultaneously is a rare marker of dominance, and cements Gill's standing as India's ODI batting spearhead heading into a busy 2026-27 international calendar.
depth.ripple_effects: The rankings boost strengthens Gill's case as a long-term ODI leadership figure for India and adds to the commercial and selection momentum behind both him and Siraj; Suryavanshi's rapid rise keeps fueling talk of an early India call-up.
depth.why_now: This is a scheduled ICC rankings update reflecting results from India's just-concluded ODI series in England.
depth.watch_next: Watch whether Gill can hold the top spot through India's next ODI assignments, and whether Suryavanshi's rankings surge translates into a senior India call-up.

key_terms.definition: A points-based system the International Cricket Council uses to rank players in each format, updated after each series based on performance and the strength of the opposition.

cards.title: Bumrah's Sri Lanka Test fate now hinges on an August 7 practice match in Colombo
cards.what_happened: New reporting details the specific mechanism that will decide whether **Bumrah** plays in India's upcoming Sri Lanka Test series: a **practice match in Colombo beginning August 7** is now understood to be the actual test of his readiness, rather than a simple fitness scan. That leaves only **eight days** between that practice match and the first Test, which starts **August 15 in Galle** (the second Test follows August 23 in Colombo). Bumrah has been resting his knee since injuring it fielding in the second ODI against England at Cardiff, with medical staff advising a full rest period until **July 30** before he reports to the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence** in Bengaluru for rehab and reassessment. All-rounder **Ravindra Jadeja**, who had also been on a fitness watch after an IPL 2026 elbow injury, has already been cleared and is back in the squad.
key_points: A **practice match in Colombo starting August 7** will be the real decider on Bumrah's fitness
That's just **eight days** before the first Test begins in **Galle on August 15**
Bumrah hurt his knee fielding in the **second ODI vs England** in Cardiff; swelling ruled him out of the third
He was told to **rest until July 30**, then report to the BCCI's **Centre of Excellence** in Bengaluru
**Ravindra Jadeja** has already been declared fit and is back in the squad after IPL 2026 elbow trouble
cards.moot: In elite sport, a 'fitness call' is rarely a single yes/no medical decision — it usually comes down to a specific, high-pressure test event with a tight runway, which is why injury updates often stay uncertain until the last moment.

thread.previously: As of two days ago, Bumrah was resting his injured knee until July 30 before reporting to the BCCI's Centre of Excellence for a fitness scan, with multiple reports suggesting he was unlikely to be fit in time for the two-Test series starting August 15 in Galle.
thread.changed: It has now emerged that a practice match in Colombo starting August 7 — just eight days before the series opener — will be the real test of his fitness, leaving a very tight window to build match fitness before Galle.

depth.background: Jasprit Bumrah is India's premier fast bowler, and his fitness has been carefully managed for years due to a history of back and workload issues. He picked up a knee injury while fielding during the second ODI against England in Cardiff, and it worsened enough to rule him out of the following match. India's squad for the upcoming two-Test tour of Sri Lanka — captained by Shubman Gill, with KL Rahul as deputy — was already named on July 26, with Bumrah included but explicitly marked as fitness-dependent, and Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna named as pace backups in case he isn't ready.
depth.why_it_matters: Bumrah is India's most important bowler in Test cricket, and his availability significantly changes the balance of the bowling attack — if he's ruled out, India would lean more heavily on Mohammed Siraj and Prasidh Krishna against a Sri Lankan side on home conditions.
depth.ripple_effects: If the tight timeline means Bumrah isn't fully match-fit, team management may manage his workload carefully even if he is included, similar to past tours — potentially resting him for the second Test to protect him for future series. It also raises the profile of back-up pacers who'll need to step up if he's unavailable.
depth.why_now: This surfaces now because the specific fitness-test mechanism (the August 7 Colombo practice match) has only just been reported, sharpening the timeline beyond the general 'rest until July 30' guidance given previously.
depth.watch_next: How Bumrah performs and how much he bowls in that August 7 Colombo practice match — it will be the clearest signal of his Test availability.

cards.title: Barbados holds Sir Garfield Sobers' state funeral at Kensington Oval
cards.what_happened: Following days of public mourning — with Sobers's body lying in state first at Barbados's Parliament on July 27, then at Kensington Oval on July 28 — the island held his official state funeral on Wednesday, July 29, at 10am. The service comprised a public thanksgiving ceremony at Kensington Oval, the ground where he built much of his legend, followed by a private funeral at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens in Christ Church. The government made free public tickets available across the island for those wanting to attend in person, and the ceremony was also livestreamed via the Barbados Parliament's official channel for those who couldn't.
key_points: Barbados held a **state funeral** for Sir Garfield Sobers at Kensington Oval on Wednesday at **10am**
The service included a **public thanksgiving** at the Oval, followed by a **private funeral** at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens
Free public tickets were distributed islandwide, with the service also carried on a **livestream**
Sobers, who died at **89**, lay in state at Parliament on July 27 and at Kensington Oval on July 28
A state funeral is among the **highest honours** Barbados can bestow, reflecting his status as a National Hero
cards.moot: The honours a nation gives its sporting greats say as much about a sport's cultural weight as any statistic ever could.

thread.previously: We reported Sobers's body was lying in state at Kensington Oval on July 28, ahead of a state funeral confirmed for Wednesday, July 29, at 10am.
thread.changed: That state funeral has now actually taken place — the public thanksgiving at Kensington Oval followed by a private service at Coral Ridge Memorial Gardens.

depth.background: Sir Garfield Sobers is widely regarded as the greatest all-rounder in cricket history — a batter, bowler and fielder who redefined what one player could do on a cricket field during his career with the West Indies. He was Barbados's first National Hero to receive this level of state honour tied so directly to his sport, and Kensington Oval is the very ground most associated with his legend, making it the natural site for the public to say goodbye.
depth.why_it_matters: It closes out a national period of mourning for a figure Barbadians and the wider West Indies consider a defining national and sporting icon — the scale of the state's response reflects how central cricket is to Caribbean identity.
depth.ripple_effects: Expect tributes across world cricket in the coming days, and potential permanent memorials — stand renamings, statues, or similar honours — at Kensington Oval or elsewhere in Barbados.
depth.why_now: This was the scheduled date for the state funeral, confirmed by the Barbadian government days earlier.

cards.title: West Indies beat Pakistan by 90 runs in the Trinidad Test to take a 1-0 series lead
cards.what_happened: West Indies beat Pakistan by **90 runs** in the first Test at the Brian Lara Stadium in Tarouba, Trinidad, taking a **1-0 lead** in the two-match series. Chasing **211** for victory, Pakistan collapsed to **120 all out**, with **Jayden Seales** taking **5 for 20** to finish the innings, trapping Mohammad Abbas leg-before as the last wicket. **Babar Azam** was the lone resistance, finishing unbeaten on **58**. Earlier, West Indies had posted **311** in their first innings (Shai Hope 92, Kavem Hodge 84), before Pakistan replied with **282** (Shan Masood 109), with **Justin Greaves** taking **5 for 27** as Pakistan lost seven wickets for just 38 runs in a middle-order collapse. West Indies were then bowled out for **181** in their second innings — themselves reduced to 93 for 7 by Mohammad Abbas's **5 for 22** — before Shamar Joseph's late 38 off 27 balls set Pakistan's target.
key_points: West Indies won the **first Test** by **90 runs** at Trinidad's Brian Lara Stadium.
**Jayden Seales** took **5 for 20** in Pakistan's second innings, sealing the win.
Pakistan, set **211** to win, were bowled out for just **120**; Babar Azam was unbeaten on **58**.
**Justin Greaves'** 5-for-27 had earlier ripped through Pakistan's first innings, which fell for **282**.
West Indies now lead the **two-match series 1-0**.
cards.moot: In Test cricket, a match can swing entirely on a handful of key bowling spells — West Indies' two 5-wicket hauls, not their batting, decided this result.

depth.background: Pakistan came into this series after a poor recent run in overseas Test cricket, and this match — the first of a two-Test series against West Indies — was an early test of whether that pattern would continue. Jayden Seales and Justin Greaves have both emerged as key parts of a young West Indies pace attack over the past two years, and this match showcased both of them delivering match-defining spells with the ball on a pitch that offered real assistance to fast bowling throughout.
depth.why_it_matters: The win extends Pakistan's struggles in away Test cricket and gives a young West Indies side — built around emerging fast bowlers like Seales and Greaves — a genuine statement result heading into the second Test.
depth.ripple_effects: A series win here would be West Indies' first Test series victory over Pakistan in years, a meaningful marker for a team trying to rebuild its Test-cricket credibility, and would add fresh pressure on Pakistan's team management over their overseas form.
depth.why_now: The Test concluded on its fourth day as West Indies completed the win.
depth.watch_next: The second and final Test of the series, where Pakistan will look to level the series and West Indies will aim to close it out.

cards.title: Smriti Mandhana's unbeaten 88 fires Manchester Super Giants past Sunrisers Leeds in a Hundred thriller
cards.what_happened: Sunrisers Leeds posted **142** batting first at Headingley, with useful innings from Phoebe Litchfield (31 off 26), Annabel Sutherland (35 off 24), and captain Dani Gibson (18 off 6). In reply, **Smriti Mandhana** took the chase away from Leeds almost single-handedly, racing to a half-century off just **33 balls** before finishing unbeaten on **88 off 50 balls**, including two sixes in the final over to seal the win. Manchester Super Giants got home with **4 wickets and 5 balls to spare**. Mandhana was named Player of the Match for her innings, which also included two catches in the field.

depth.background: **The Hundred** is England's 100-ball franchise cricket tournament, running men's and women's competitions in parallel each summer, and has become a regular stop for top international players like India's **Smriti Mandhana**, one of the world's leading women's batters. This was the **10th match** of the 2026 Women's Competition, played at Headingley in Leeds between hosts Sunrisers Leeds and Manchester Super Giants.
depth.why_it_matters: It's a statement innings from one of the world's premier women's batters in one of the sport's most-watched franchise leagues, the kind of performance that boosts both Mandhana's and the tournament's profile ahead of India's own busy cricket calendar.
depth.ripple_effects: Strong overseas form for Indian players in leagues like The Hundred typically feeds into selection conversations and form heading into international series, and helps grow the commercial profile of women's cricket globally.
